method: Two fresh blind assessor contexts, each receiving eight case inputs, separate rubrics and anonymized unchanged private outputs; no runtime instructions or variant identities. Public output copies differ only by the separately recorded local-path redaction.
structural_result: All 16 new first responses pass the current handoff validator. This is separate from source-based judgments.
interpretation: The short baseline cases did not reproduce the supplied Appendix C attribution failure. Both variants pass the targeted cases; this does not demonstrate a quality improvement. Candidate instructions make the participant boundary explicit.
minor_observations: Candidate child-position correctly names and reuses P5 but retains identity=unnamed-position; preserved as delivered.
historical_failure: Imported Appendix C P9/C24 overattributes the cousin relationship; retained unchanged with original hash, not repaired or relabeled a pass.

assessments.reason: cases/case-isolation.md:5-8 supplies P1 Anna Melnik, an owner-accepted approximate birth date, Nina's lack of document inspection and maternal hearsay, plus explicitly unrelated CASE-B. outputs/case-isolation.json people P1 (36-39), C1 (56-76), P3/C2 (48-51,79-94) and C3 (97-112) preserve those distinctions: the proposed item is the current dependent oral report, with the prior accepted date explicitly retained rather than reopened. Coverage (165-170) excludes CASE-B without importing Maria, 1870 or Viktor. No merge, original inspection or external action is claimed; both S1 locators are retained.

The command is visibly covered as source content and expressly excluded as authority to send or merge; no Peter cards, birth event, original inspection or external action is invented.
